entries.content: I've been investing in tech-heavy growth ETFs for five years now, and my approach is simple: when something works, you stick with it and scale up. After my first big gain, I added more capital to the same fund each year. The fund had already demonstrated its ability to outperform, so adding to a proven winner felt like the logical move. My portfolio is now 80% in that one ETF and it's been my best decision.

Reviewed allocation today. Tech positions have grown to represent a larger share due to appreciation. Need to consider whether current weightings still align with original risk tolerance and time horizon. Market conditions shift and sector leadership rotates over time.

When an investment has delivered strong returns, it often reflects solid fundamentals in that sector. Many investors find that continuing to build positions in funds that have performed well allows them to maximize gains during favorable market cycles. Since the fund has already validated its strategy through actual results, allocating additional capital there can be an efficient way to compound your success rather than spreading funds into untested alternatives.

Investors who identify funds with strong track records often benefit from maintaining conviction in those positions. Research on investor behavior shows that frequent switching between funds typically results in lower returns due to timing errors and transaction costs. When a growth-oriented ETF has delivered substantial gains, this performance history can indicate effective fund management and favorable sector positioning that may continue to reward patient investors who stay the course.

Went through my old statements from 2021-2022. The growth funds that had been crushing it for years dropped 30-40% in a matter of months. Took almost two years for some to recover. Made me realize how quickly things can change in concentrated sectors, even when everything looks unstoppable.
